questions.question: Rates of surgical site infections have been increasing in your institution. You are on a committee asked to examine methods to improve surgical site infection rates.
questions.question_raw: Rates of surgical site infections have been increasing in your institution. You are a part of a committee that has been asked to examine methods to improve rates of surgical site infections.

parts.text: Give 4 recommendations to include as part of your prevention bundle.

parts_raw.text: What are 4 recommendations to make as part of your "bundle"?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Administer prophylactic antibiotics only when indicated (appropriate drug and weight-based dose), timed to achieve tissue levels above the MIC at the time of incision, with redosing during prolonged procedures. (2) Avoid razor shaving; if hair removal is needed, delay until the time of surgery and use electric clippers or depilatories. (3) Prepare skin with an alcohol-based antiseptic agent (e.g., chlorhexidine-alcohol) unless contraindicated. (4) Maintain perioperative normothermia (core temperature at or above 36.0 degrees C) and perioperative euglycemia (glucose below 200 mg/dL through the second postoperative day) in both diabetic and non-diabetic patients.

cohort_answer.text: Administer preoperative abx only when indicated based on published clinical practice guidelines and timed such that a bactericidal concentration of the agents is established in the serum and tissues when the incision is made; Ensure perioperative glycemic control; Maintain perioperative normothermia; Advise patient to shower/bathe with soap/antiseptic agent at least the night before operation; Intraop skin prep with an alcohol based antiseptic agent unless contraindicated; Don't shave patient – appropriate hair removal; Minimize duration of procedure. (JAMA Surgery: https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamasurgery/fullarticle/2623725)

questions.question: List strategies to reduce surgical site infections.

parts.text: List 5 strategies to reduce surgical site infections.

parts_raw.text: 5 strategies to reduced surgical site infections

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Timely, appropriately dosed prophylactic antibiotics with intraoperative redosing when the procedure is prolonged. (2) Avoid razors; if hair removal is required, use clippers/depilatories at the time of surgery. (3) Alcohol-based skin antiseptic preparation (e.g., chlorhexidine-alcohol) unless contraindicated. (4) Maintain perioperative normothermia (core temperature 36.0 degrees C or higher) and provide supplemental oxygen in intubated patients with normal pulmonary function. (5) Maintain perioperative glycemic control (glucose below 200 mg/dL) and consider S. aureus decolonization with intranasal mupirocin plus CHG for cardiac and arthroplasty procedures.

questions.question: A person who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting with a saphenous vein graft harvest keeps developing recurrent cellulitis with fever in the harvest limb. [image-based question: leg cellulitis, image not needed]
questions.question_raw: PM 18. Person post CABG with saphenous vein graft keeps getting cellulitis with fever (picture shown, not needed)

parts.text: Name the most common causative organism.
How do you prevent recurrent infection? Give 3 examples.

parts_raw.text: What is the most common organism? (1)
How do you prevent the infection? Give 3 examples. (1.5)

questions.model_answer:
a) Beta-hemolytic streptococci (particularly group A, and group C/G streptococci); this is the classic cause of recurrent cellulitis in the lymphatically compromised saphenous vein harvest limb.
b) (1) Manage limb edema and lymphedema with compression stockings and leg elevation. (2) Meticulous skin care and treatment/eradication of tinea pedis and other portals of entry (interdigital fissures). (3) For frequent recurrences (roughly 3 or more episodes per year despite the above), long-term suppressive prophylaxis with penicillin V 250-500 mg PO BID (or oral amoxicillin/erythromycin if penicillin-allergic).
questions.beyond_mandell: Recurrent post-vein-harvest cellulitis and its streptococcal etiology/prophylaxis are covered by the IDSA 2014 skin and soft tissue infection guidelines, not this SSI prophylaxis chapter.

cohort_answer.text: Beta hemolytic strep (Group C strep/Group A strep). Prevention: Compression stocking for edema management, skin care and treatment of tinea if present, elevation, diuretics; if >3 episodes/year consider prophylactic antibiotics (penicillin V 500mg BID, amox 250-500mg BID).

questions.question: Surgical site infection prevention bundles.

parts.text: List 5 routinely recommended interventions in a bundled package to decrease surgical site infections.

parts_raw.text: List 5 routinely recommended interventions in bundled package to decrease surgical site infections

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Avoid razors for hair removal (delay removal to time of surgery; use clippers or depilatories only if necessary). (2) Maintain perioperative normothermia (core temperature 36.0 degrees C or higher). (3) Use an alcohol-based skin preparation combined with chlorhexidine gluconate. (4) Decolonize with intranasal antistaphylococcal agents (mupirocin) plus chlorhexidine bathing for high-risk procedures (cardiac and arthroplasty). (5) Maintain perioperative euglycemia (glucose below 200 mg/dL through the second postoperative day) in diabetic and non-diabetic patients, and give timely, correctly dosed prophylactic antibiotics with redosing.

cohort_answer.text: Avoiding razors for hair removal; Maintaining normothermia; Use of chlorhexidine gluconate plus alcohol-based skin preparation agents; Decolonization with intranasal antistaphylococcal agents and antistaphylococcal skin antiseptics for high-risk procedures (cardiothoracic and orthopedic); Maintaining euglycemia in the postoperative period; Using negative pressure wound therapy (JAMA - evidence for these interventions)
